# isSymbolAlias

> Test if an input value is a supported [symbol alias][@stdlib/plot/base/symbol-aliases].

<!-- Section to include introductory text. Make sure to keep an empty line after the intro `section` element and another before the `/section` close. -->

<section class="intro">

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<!-- Package usage documentation. -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var isSymbolAlias = require( '@stdlib/plot/base/assert/is-symbol-alias' );
```

#### isSymbolAlias( value )

Tests if an input value is a supported [symbol alias][@stdlib/plot/base/symbol-aliases].

```javascript
var bool = isSymbolAlias( 'circle' );
// returns true

bool = isSymbolAlias( 'foo' );
// returns false
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<!-- Package usage notes. Make sure to keep an empty line after the `section` element and another before the `/section` close. -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   An alias is the human-readable name of a symbol (e.g., `circle`), as opposed to a [shorthand][@stdlib/plot/base/symbol-shorthands] (e.g., `o`).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<!-- Package usage examples. -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var isSymbolAlias = require( '@stdlib/plot/base/assert/is-symbol-alias' );

var bool = isSymbolAlias( 'circle' );
// returns true

bool = isSymbolAlias( 'triangle-up' );
// returns true

bool = isSymbolAlias( '' );
// returns false

bool = isSymbolAlias( 'foo' );
// returns false
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
